description: How a ToolCall is presented to Cedar: the 2026-07-27 enterprise demo's vocabulary — Action::"invoke_tool" on ToolUse::"<tool>" with the arguments under context.tool_args — now declared on the chain instead of coded in the engine. `model` reads the gateway's normalized `gatewayContext.model` observation; both it and `tool_args` are optional on the Kind, so an instance that omits them simply presents no such key. Spec 011 §11 (KS-7): every act now carries the actor's standing into the context — `identity` says whether the request was signed, and `authority_roots` names the keys its cited authority resolves to. Both are the kernel's own answers, settled before `authorize` runs and recorded on the receipt, so a rule written against them decides on the same facts a reader of the chain will see. The field they replace, `@actor.keyFingerprint`, was a fingerprint the actor asserted about itself and is removed from the grammar. R1-F4 (RC review 2026-09-05): `principal_source` is the gateway's own answer about where the client identity came from (`jwt`, `client_metadata`, `mtls_svid`, `anonymous`), so a rule can refuse an anonymous principal; it says how the gateway got the name, never that the name was authenticated.
